Structure follows elt.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; blanco: title, telescope (machine-readable primary, pupil, foci; refs point to sourced params as "blanco.<param>"), explorer_preset (the proposed web/tpresets.js entry), params, not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.rule: Each value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/blanco/. derived = arithmetic or a measurement done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values. INFERRED marks a reasoned guess no source states. NOT FOUND marks a gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_normalization: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), degree-like glyphs, division slash, tilde operator, approximately-equal sign, middle dot, plus-minus (to +/-), no-break space and soft hyphen normalized; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes against the text with PDF line-end hyphenation removed or closed up, or with all whitespace removed; " ... " joins non-adjacent pieces.
_meta.texts_checked: pdftotext -layout and -raw per page and across consecutive page pairs (PDF p. = page index of the saved PDF); HTML as tag-stripped text (tags to a space, tags removed) and raw source (UTF-8); .py and .yaml as is; FITS headers as 80-character cards.

decam_corrector.derived: Table 1 spacings from C1 to the focal plane sum to 1906.155 mm, so the focal plane lies 8875.037 + 1906.155 = 10781.19 mm above the primary's vertex, 125.39 mm beyond the primary's own focus (10655.8 mm). The filter-changer housing lies along +/-x, the fins at 45, 135, 225 (the wide one) and 315 deg. batoid and Piff's DECam_pupil_512.fits show the same pupil turned 90 deg (housing along y).

One pupil serves every focus since 2012: the f/8 secondary mounts on the front of the DECam cage (F15 Sec. 2.8), so the cage shadow, the fins and (INFERRED) the filter-changer housing shadow the Cassegrain beam as well. The historical foci are drawn without the housing (pupil.blocks = []).

The f/8, f/14.5 and f/30 focal lengths and focus positions come from a paraxial two-mirror trace of the BOP prescription; the imager.js Cassegrain model, given F, F1 and back, reproduces the published mirror spacings to 0.01 mm (scratch script).
Collecting areas: BOP's 10.014 m^2 counts only the 1651 mm obstruction; the explorer pupil (fins and housing) has 9.311 m^2 (DERIVED).
